sections.section_name: Section B - Theory Short Answer Concepts

questions.question_text: Define 'Still Life' drawing and name two everyday objects that could be used for a still life composition. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Still life drawing is the art of depicting inanimate, everyday objects arranged together. Common objects used include a bowl of fruits and a flower vase.

questions.question_text: Briefly explain the role of 'Taal' in Indian music. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Taal is the rhythmic cycle in Indian music that organizes time into specific beats, providing a structured framework for musicians and dancers to follow during a performance.

questions.question_text: How can music effectively portray different human emotions? Give one example. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Music portrays emotions through variations in tempo, pitch, and instruments. For example, a slow, soft melody on a flute can evoke sadness or calmness, while fast, loud drums create excitement.

questions.question_text: What is the basic difference between a string instrument (Chordophone) and a wind instrument (Aerophone)? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: String instruments produce sound by plucking or bowing stretched strings (like a guitar), while wind instruments create sound by blowing air into a tube or mouthpiece (like a flute).

questions.question_text: Describe the technique of block printing using natural objects like leaves or vegetables. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: In natural block printing, a vegetable half (like a potato) or a leaf is dipped in wet paint and pressed firmly onto paper or fabric to transfer its distinct texture and shape.

sections.section_name: Section C - Practical Tasks: Composition & Observation

questions.question_text: Observe and draw a composition of a closed book with a pair of reading glasses resting on top of it. Use pencil shading to show depth and texture. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Assess the correct perspective of the rectangular book and the structural proportion of the glasses. Marks are awarded for accurate light source direction, smooth gradient shading using B-grade pencils, crisp drop shadows beneath the book, and delicate reflections on the glass lenses.

questions.question_text: Draw a traditional Indian musical instrument (e.g., Tabla or Sitar) demonstrating accurate structural proportions and realistic details of its strings or tuning blocks. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Grading focuses on the symmetrical structure of the instrument body. For a Tabla, the intricate lacing and center black spot (syahi) must be detailed. For a Sitar, the frets and tuning pegs must be proportionately aligned, accompanied by varied tonal shading.

sections.section_name: Section D - Practical Tasks: Applied Design & Messaging

questions.question_text: Create a repeating geometric pattern suitable for a textile block print border. Use only three contrasting colors to fill the design. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The design must show a clear, continuous rhythmic repetition of geometric shapes (triangles, squares, or circles) without breaking the sequence. Marks are awarded for precision in linework, strict adherence to the three-color limit, and the overall visual balance and striking contrast of the chosen color palette.

questions.question_text: Design a visually appealing poster for a school 'Music Festival'. Include a bold title, an illustration of musical notes or instruments, and vibrant coloring using watercolors or poster colors. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The poster requires legible, stylized typography for the title. The central illustration must effectively integrate musical symbols with dynamic energy. High marks are given for the neat application of wet mediums (watercolors/poster colors), preventing muddy overlaps, and ensuring the layout visually communicates a festive musical atmosphere.
